reason: The only production change narrows the AF_INET6 comparison in the internal static helper ares_addr_equal from the enclosing addr6 object to its _S6_un._S6_u8 byte array, avoiding padding. H0 exclusively invokes ares_parse_*_reply entry points and has no server address, cookie state, or API path that reaches or controls ares_addr_equal. However, this lack of reachability is historical in both S0 + H0 and S1 + H0; the commit adds no entry point, protocol, state, configuration, input semantics, or attack surface and does not materially aggravate the existing separation. It is an internal comparison correction, so no commit-induced harness maintenance is needed.
evidence: H0 calls only ares_parse_a_reply, ares_parse_aaaa_reply, ares_parse_ptr_reply, ares_parse_ns_reply, ares_parse_srv_reply, ares_parse_mx_reply, ares_parse_txt_reply, ares_parse_soa_reply, ares_parse_naptr_reply, ares_parse_caa_reply, and ares_parse_uri_reply.

For AF_INET6, S0 compares sizeof(addr1->addr.addr6) bytes while S1 compares sizeof(addr1->addr.addr6._S6_un._S6_u8) bytes; the surrounding family check, AF_INET handling, and return behavior are unchanged.
No new or changed public declaration, callable entry point, state transition, configuration control, or input format appears in the supplied production diff.
recommended_action: Keep H0 unchanged for this commit; assess cookie/server-address logic under a separate harness only as broader historical coverage work.
